=== shi2025_closer_look.yaml ===
paper_key: "shi2025_closer_look"
title: "A Closer Look at Model Collapse: From a Generalization-to-Memorization Perspective"
venue: "NeurIPS 2025 (Spotlight)"
full_text_available: true

research:
  baselines:
    - "Vanilla replace paradigm (train on synthetic data only)"
    - "Vanilla accumulate-subsample paradigm (uniform subsampling from real + all synthetic)"
    - "Unconditional DDPM generation"
    - "Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG, scale=2)"
  metrics:
    - {name: "Generalization Score (GS)", direction: "higher_better", definition: "Average L2 distance in DINOv2 feature space between each generated image and its nearest training neighbor"}
    - {name: "FID (Frechet Inception Distance)", direction: "lower_better", definition: "InceptionV3-based distribution distance"}
    - {name: "Estimated Entropy (Kozachenko-Leonenko)", direction: "higher_better", definition: "KL entropy estimator with gamma=1 on DINOv2 features"}
  datasets:
    - {name: "CIFAR-10", size: "32,768 images (32x32)", note: "Also used nested subsets: 1024/2048/4096/8192/16384/32768"}
    - {name: "FFHQ", size: "8,192 images (downsampled to 32x32)"}
    - {name: "MNIST", size: "12,000 images"}
  ablation_dimensions:
    - "Dataset size (1024 to 32768 in powers of 2)"
    - "Training paradigm (replace vs accumulate-subsample)"
    - "Selection method (Greedy Selection vs Threshold Decay Filter vs vanilla)"
    - "Number of generated candidates (N vs 2N before selection)"
    - "Threshold decay rate alpha (sensitivity analysis)"
    - "Classifier-Free Guidance scale"
    - "Entropy vs variance as correlation target"
  training_recipe:
    model: "UNet-based DDPM (~16-19M parameters)"
    optimizer: "Adam"
    lr: "1e-4"
    weight_decay: "1e-6"
    batch_size: 128
    precision: "FP16 mixed"
    diffusion_steps: 1000
    epochs_cifar: 500
    epochs_ffhq: 1000
    hardware: "Single NVIDIA A100 GPU"
    feature_extractor: "DINOv2 (for distance/entropy computation)"
    unet_channels_cifar_ffhq: "[48, 48, 96, 96, 144, 144] with 6 down/up blocks"
    unet_channels_mnist: "[64, 128, 256, 512] with 4 down/up blocks"
  method_family: "Entropy-based data selection for mitigating model collapse in iterative generative training"

positioning:
  core_claim: "Model collapse in diffusion models manifests as a generalization-to-memorization transition driven by training data entropy shrinkage, not just variance collapse — and entropy-based data selection can effectively delay this transition."
  key_results: >
    Pearson r=0.91 between training data entropy and log(generalization score), dataset-size-independent.
    FFHQ accumulate-subsample: vanilla FID=75.7 vs Greedy Selection FID=44.7 at iteration 8.
    MNIST CFG: vanilla CFG FID=66.2 vs CFG+filtering FID=22.4 at iteration 8.
    Greedy Selection preferentially retains real data (65% real by iteration 8 vs 12.5% uniform baseline).
  limitations:
    - "No rigorous theoretical explanation for why entropy collapses — only empirical demonstration"
    - "Limited to image diffusion models; no validation on language models or discrete diffusion"
    - "Greedy Selection is computationally expensive (quadratic in dataset size)"
    - "Only tested on 32x32 resolution images with relatively small models (~16-19M params)"
    - "No formal analysis of how many iterations can be sustained before memorization"
  relation_to_us: "foundation"

narrative:
  story_type: "突破局限型"
  hook: >
    Opens with the practical inevitability of synthetic data contamination: as diffusion models flood
    the internet with generated content, future training sets will inevitably contain synthetic data,
    creating a self-consuming loop. This is a real-world crisis framing, not hypothetical.
  tension: >
    Existing perspectives on model collapse (variance shrinkage, distribution shift) are shown to be
    theoretically valid but practically insufficient — variance collapse requires "an extremely large
    number of iterations" to manifest, making it "rarely a practical concern." This creates a gap:
    the community has mathematical frameworks that don't explain what practitioners actually observe.
  key_insight: >
    Revealed in paragraph 3 of the intro: the transition from generalization to memorization is the
    true practical manifestation of collapse. Models don't just get worse — they specifically lose the
    ability to generate novel content and start copying training data. The entropy of the training set
    (not the model) is the key diagnostic signal, with r=0.91 correlation to generalizability.
  argument_chain: >
    Real-world synthetic data contamination is inevitable →
    Existing collapse perspectives miss practical manifestations →
    We observe a generalization-to-memorization transition (Finding I) →
    Training data entropy shrinks across iterations (Finding II) →
    Entropy strongly correlates with generalization capability (Finding III, r=0.91) →
    Entropy-based data selection preserves diversity and delays collapse →
    Validated across 3 datasets, 2 paradigms, with CFG extension
  contribution_framing: >
    Three numbered contributions, each one sentence. Pattern: identify phenomenon → investigate
    driving factor → propose and validate mitigation. Clean problem-insight-solution structure.
    Contributions are framed as empirical discoveries rather than theoretical claims, matching the
    paper's predominantly experimental nature.
  intro_structure: >
    3 paragraphs + "Our Contributions" subsection.
    P1: Problem context — synthetic data proliferation and the self-consuming loop threat.
    P2: Critique of existing perspectives — variance collapse and distribution shift are insufficient.
    P3: Their perspective — generalization-to-memorization transition, entropy as diagnostic, proposed mitigation.
    Contributions: 3 numbered items following identify-investigate-propose pattern.
  notable_technique: >
    The paper uses a "practical insufficiency" argument to distinguish itself from prior theoretical
    work. Instead of claiming predecessors are wrong, it argues they are right but miss what matters
    in practice. This is a diplomatically effective positioning that avoids direct conflict while
    establishing clear novelty. The visual pairing of generated images with their nearest training
    neighbors (Figure 2 left) makes the abstract concept of "memorization" viscerally obvious.

  figure_count: 9
  figure1:
    type: "method_overview"
    description: >
      Three-row pipeline diagram. Top row (green background): "Collapse Iteration" showing the
      replace paradigm where D1 → Training → M1 → Sampling → D2 → Training → M2 → ... → Dn.
      Middle row (blue background): "Mitigated Iteration" showing the accumulate-subsample paradigm
      with a pie chart merging real data and previously generated data, plus a funnel icon for
      "Selection" before constructing D2. Bottom right (orange background): "Evolution" panel showing
      pairs of generated images (top) and their nearest training counterparts (bottom) at Iterations
      1, 3, and n, with a horizontal arrow from "Generalization" to "Memorization" and "Degradation"
      labels between iteration pairs.
    narrative_role: >
      Serves as the roadmap for the entire paper: defines the two paradigms (collapse vs mitigated),
      introduces the selection intervention, and previews the core finding (generalization-to-memorization
      transition) — all in one figure. The reader immediately grasps the problem, the setup, and the
      paper's contribution.
    design_elements:
      - "Color-coded rows: green=collapse, blue=mitigated, orange=evolution"
      - "Pipeline arrows connecting dataset→model→sampling→dataset"
      - "Pie chart for data composition (real vs synthetic)"
      - "Funnel icon for selection step"
      - "Real face image pairs showing degradation progression"
      - "Horizontal arrow from Generalization to Memorization"
    visual_style: >
      Clean horizontal flow with three visually distinct rows. Pastel background colors (green,
      blue, orange) separate conceptual layers. Neural network icons for models, cylindrical icons
      for datasets. The bottom-right evolution panel uses real face images to ground the abstract
      pipeline in concrete visual evidence. Legend in bottom-left defines notation.
  result_figures:
    - figure_id: "Figure 2"
      viz_type: "qualitative_comparison + line_plot"
      what_compared: "Generated images vs their nearest training neighbors across iterations 1, 3, 8; GS decay curves for 6 dataset sizes"
      how_gain_highlighted: "Left panel shows progressive visual convergence (memorization). Right panel uses color-coded curves with labeled 'Generalization Regime' and 'Memorization Regime' regions."
      design_note: >
        Powerful dual-panel design: qualitative evidence (left) paired with quantitative curves (right).
        The image grid makes memorization viscerally obvious — generated faces become identical to

        annotated text labels for the two regions. Six dataset sizes in distinct colors show the

    - figure_id: "Figure 4a"

      how_gain_highlighted: "Red dashed regression line through all points from all dataset sizes, demonstrating r=0.91 universal correlation. Points from different sizes align on the same line."
      design_note: >
        The key evidence figure. Log-scale y-axis linearizes the relationship. Color coding by dataset
        size (same palette as Figure 2) shows that different sizes fall on the same line — establishing
        a dataset-size-independent law. Clean white background, no clutter. Contrast with Figure 4b
        (variance) where the correlation is visibly weaker.
    - figure_id: "Figure 5"
      viz_type: "multi_panel_line_plot"
      what_compared: "Generalization Score over iterations for vanilla vs Greedy Selection vs Threshold Decay Filter, across datasets and paradigms"
      how_gain_highlighted: "Three lines per panel; selection methods consistently above vanilla, showing sustained higher GS"
      design_note: "6 subfigures in a grid (datasets x paradigms). Independent y-axes per subfigure to show relative improvement. Clean legend with three line styles."
    - figure_id: "Figure 6"
      viz_type: "multi_panel_line_plot"
      what_compared: "FID over iterations for vanilla vs Greedy Selection vs Threshold Decay Filter"
      how_gain_highlighted: "Selection methods consistently lower FID curves than vanilla across all panels"
      design_note: "Same grid layout as Figure 5 for parallel reading. FID improvement most dramatic on accumulate-subsample paradigm."
    - figure_id: "Figure 8"
      viz_type: "stacked_bar_chart_with_overlay_line"
      what_compared: "Proportion of selected images from each iteration source; blue bars = real data proportion vs red 1/n baseline line"
      how_gain_highlighted: "Blue bars (real data fraction) dramatically exceed the red 1/n line, especially in later iterations — the method naturally discovers that real data is more diverse"
      design_note: >
        Insightful visualization of an emergent behavior: the selection algorithm was not told to prefer
        real data, but the entropy-maximizing objective naturally selects more real images as synthetic
        data clusters tighten. The stacked bars show composition while the overlay line shows the
        null expectation. Multiple panels for different datasets/methods.
    - figure_id: "Figure 9"
      viz_type: "qualitative_comparison + line_plot"
      what_compared: "MNIST generation: unconditional (FID=74.4) vs CFG (FID=66.2) vs CFG+filtering (FID=22.4)"
      how_gain_highlighted: "Side-by-side digit grids show dramatic quality improvement; entropy plot shows filtering maintains diversity that CFG alone destroys"
      design_note: "Extension experiment demonstrating generality beyond unconditional setting. The 3x improvement in FID (66.2→22.4) is a compelling headline number."
  ablation_figures:
    - figure_id: "Figure 3"
      viz_type: "line_plot + 2D_scatter_projection"
      dimensions_varied: ["iteration number", "dataset entropy"]
      design_note: >
        Three-panel figure. Left: entropy decay curves over iterations for different dataset sizes.
        Middle and Right: 2D SVD projections of data distribution at iteration 1 (spread) vs
        iteration 21 (collapsed into tight clusters). The SVD projections make entropy collapse
        visually intuitive — you can see the distribution concentrating.
    - figure_id: "Figure 7"
      viz_type: "multi_panel_line_plot"
      dimensions_varied: ["selection method", "training paradigm", "dataset"]
      design_note: "Shows that selection methods maintain higher entropy across iterations. Same grid layout as Figures 5-6 for parallel comparison. Entropy serves as the mechanistic explanation for why GS and FID improve."
    - figure_id: "Figure 4b"
      viz_type: "scatter"
      dimensions_varied: ["variance vs generalization score as alternative to entropy"]
      design_note: "Deliberately placed next to Figure 4a to show that variance is a weaker predictor than entropy. The scatter is visibly more dispersed, making the entropy superiority obvious without needing statistics."
  figure_narrative_role: >
    Figure 1 (pipeline overview + generalization-to-memorization preview) →
    Figure 2 (Finding I: generalization-to-memorization transition, qualitative + quantitative) →
    Figure 3 (Finding II: entropy shrinkage + distribution collapse visualization) →
    Figure 4 (Finding III: entropy-GS correlation, the key evidence; entropy vs variance comparison) →
    Figures 5-7 (Mitigation results: GS/FID/entropy improvements with selection methods, parallel grid layout) →
    Figure 8 (Mechanistic insight: selection naturally prefers real data) →
    Figure 9 (Extension: CFG setting on MNIST).
    The flow follows a clear discover-understand-mitigate-extend arc.

  key_results: "E_test = B + V + zeta decomposition where zeta is irreducible collapse term; in scaling laws regime (phi->0+), zeta ~ p2^2 * tr(Delta) remains bounded unless p2->0; 1% synthetic data sufficient to cause collapse plateau; larger models amplify collapse when real/synthetic distributions differ significantly; double-descent pattern where over-parameterized models (past m=n threshold) partially mitigate but do not eliminate collapse"

The natural hope is that diluting synthetic data with sufficient real data would restore normal scaling — this paper proves that hope is false."
  key_insight: "The key insight is the bias-variance decomposition E_test = B + V + zeta, where zeta is an irreducible collapse term that persists as long as the synthetic data fraction p2 remains fixed (non-vanishing). 6

Continuous/ordinal scoring replacing binary (EditLens, CLOC). Detection-as-collapse-mitigation: filtering synthetic data via detectors outperforms pure human training (Drayson 2025).

14	
15	## Metrics
16	
17	**AUROC** dominant (12/25). **F1** second (6/25). **TPR@low-FPR** increasingly preferred for deployment. Two Paradigms: AUROC misleading under class imbalance, supplement with PR-AUC. Collapse: FID (4/25), perplexity (4/25).
18	
19	## Key Datasets
20	
21	Detection: MAGE (7 domains×27 LLMs), RAID (2.6M texts), PAN'24. Collapse: CIFAR-10/FFHQ/MNIST (image), Wikitext-103/BabiStories (LM). Data quality: FineWeb (15T tokens).
22	
23	## Experimental Design Consensus (6/8 deep-read)
24	
25	1. Cross-domain + cross-model eval mandatory
26	2. Paraphrasing attack robustness required (drops recall 30-40%)
27	3. Progressive difficulty testbeds (MAGE: 8 scenarios easy→hard)
28	4. Collapse: iterate 8-60 rounds with per-round FID/entropy
29	
30	## Common Limitations (cross-paper freq)
31	
32	- Short text (<100 tokens): all detectors degrade (4/8)
33	- Newest LLMs close gap: GPT-4o entropy≈human beyond 4K chars; o1 undetectable (Two Paradigms)
34	- Paraphrasing universal attack (3/8)
35	- Collapse theory assumes Gaussian/linear — practice gap (3/8)
36	
37	## Research Gaps
38	
39	- **No paper estimates recursive generation depth** — detection is binary/ternary only
40	- Detection×collapse barely connected: only Drayson bridges; no work diagnoses *how many* generations occurred
41	- Ordinal framing (EditLens, CLOC) not applied to generation depth
42	- No collapse analysis for instruction-tuned LLMs
43

# AI Text Detection & Model Collapse — Research Patterns

From 25 papers (8 deep-read, 17 abstract). Domain: LLM text detection + model collapse + data quality.

## Method Trends

**Rising** (high confidence): Zero-shot statistical scoring dominates detection — DetectGPT→Fast-DetectGPT (340x speedup)→Binoculars (>90% TPR@0.01% FPR)→DivEye (+33.2%). Continuous/ordinal scoring replacing binary (EditLens, CLOC). Detection-as-collapse-mitigation: filtering synthetic data via detectors outperforms pure human training (Drayson 2025).

**Declining**: Supervised binary classifiers fail OOD (MAGE: AUROC 0.99→0.93; Two Paradigms: attribution breaks at scale).

## Standard Baselines (citation freq)

DetectGPT (8/25) > RoBERTa (5/25) > Binoculars (4/25) > Fast-DetectGPT (4/25). New detectors must compare against Binoculars + Fast-DetectGPT as zero-shot SOTA.

## Metrics

**AUROC** dominant (12/25). **F1** second (6/25). **TPR@low-FPR** increasingly preferred for deployment. Two Paradigms: AUROC misleading under class imbalance, supplement with PR-AUC. Collapse: FID (4/25), perplexity (4/25).

## Key Datasets

Detection: **"works in lab, fails in wild"** (Ghostbuster, MAGE, Two Paradigms). Theory: **"right but practically wrong"** — prior theory valid but misses what practitioners observe (Closer Look: "variance collapse rarely a practical concern").

# AI Text Detection & Model Collapse — Research Patterns

From 25 papers (8 deep-read, 17 abstract). Domain: LLM text detection + model collapse + data quality.

## Method Trends

**Rising** (high confidence): Zero-shot statistical scoring dominates detection — DetectGPT→Fast-DetectGPT (340x speedup)→Binoculars (>90% TPR@0.01%FPR)→DivEye (+33.2%). Each successor simplifies and accelerates. Continuous/ordinal scoring replacing binary (EditLens regression, CLOC multi-margin). Detection-as-collapse-mitigation emerging: detector-filtered retraining outperforms pure human data (Drayson 2025). Verifier-based filtering shows short-term gains but converges to verifier's center (Yi 2026, Escaping Collapse).

**Declining**: Supervised binary classifiers fail OOD (MAGE: AUROC 0.99→0.93 cross-domain; Two Paradigms: attribution paradigm breaks at scale). Pure perturbation methods displaced by conditional probability approaches.

## Standard Baselines (citation freq)

DetectGPT (8/25) > RoBERTa-classifier (5/25) > Binoculars (4/25) ≈ Fast-DetectGPT (4/25) > Ghostbuster (3/25). New detectors must benchmark against Binoculars + Fast-DetectGPT as zero-shot SOTA, plus at least one supervised baseline. **Support**: 8/8 deep-read, high confidence.

## Metrics

**AUROC** dominant (12/25) but increasingly contested — Two Paradigms shows AUROC misleading under class imbalance, recommend supplementing with PR-AUC. **TPR@low-FPR** (0.01%-1%) preferred for deployment (Binoculars, Two Paradigms). **F1** for classification (6/25). Collapse domain: **FID** (4/25), **perplexity** (4/25), **test error scaling exponent** (3/25), **entropy** as diagnostic (Closer Look: r=0.91 with generalization). **Support**: 8/8, high confidence.

## Key Datasets

Detection: MAGE (7 domains×27 LLMs, 332K texts), RAID (2.6M texts, 6 LLMs), PAN'24 (15 LLMs). XSum/SQuAD/WritingPrompts = legacy trio (3/25 each). Collapse: CIFAR-10/FFHQ/MNIST for image (4/25), Wikitext-103/BabiStories for LM (2/25). Data quality: FineWeb 15T tokens, QuRating 260B.

## Experimental Design Consensus (6/8 deep-read)

1. Cross-domain + cross-model eval mandatory — in-domain results alone insufficient (MAGE, Two Paradigms, Ghostbuster)
2. Paraphrasing attack robustness required — universal weakness, recall drops 30-40% (MAGE, Ghostbuster, DivEye)
3. Progressive difficulty testbeds: easy→hard scenarios as narrative arc (MAGE: 8 testbeds; Two Paradigms: attribution→verification)
4. Collapse: iterate 8-60 rounds, report per-round FID/entropy/GS trajectory, not just final number
5. Training recipes: detection classifiers use Adam, lr~5e-3, 5 epochs on V100/A100; collapse theory uses closed-form or small DDPMs on single A100

## Common Limitations (cross-paper freq)

- Short text (<100 tokens): universal degradation (4/8 deep-read)
- Newest LLMs closing gap: GPT-4o entropy≈human beyond 4K chars; o1 undetectable by non-o1 detectors (Two Paradigms)
- Paraphrasing breaks all detectors (3/8; Ghostbuster 99%→62% recall)
- Collapse theory assumes Gaussian/linear — neural network gap acknowledged but unresolved (4/8)
- No instruction-tuned LLM collapse analysis across all papers

## Research Gaps

- **No paper estimates recursive generation depth** — detection is binary/ternary only; ordinal framing (EditLens, CLOC) exists but unapplied to depth
- Detection × collapse barely connected: only Drayson bridges; no work diagnoses *how many* generations occurred
- Strong Collapse proves mixing cannot fix collapse unless synthetic fraction→0, but no paper proposes depth-aware data curation
- Verifier quality bounds long-term performance (Yi 2026) — what if the verifier is a generation-depth estimator?

## Competitor Map

**Foundation** (9): DetectGPT, Two Paradigms, Tale of Tails, Strong Collapse, Closer Look, Broken Telephone, Ghostbuster, Demystified, survey. **Competitor** (6): MAGE, Binoculars, Fast-DetectGPT, DivEye, Intrinsic Dim, EditLens. **Complementary** (7): FineWeb, QuRating, Escaping Collapse, Drayson, Synthetic Eggs, LOKI, CLOC. **Orthogonal** (2): watermark, text degeneration.

**突破局限型 dominates** (7/8; all except FineWeb 化繁为简型). Frame contribution as overcoming a specific named prior limitation.

Three proven hooks: (1) **Real-world urgency** — cite adoption stats ("ChatGPT: 0.1% of daily global words", Tale of Tails; "schools restricting ChatGPT", Ghostbuster). (2) **Contradiction** — juxtapose success/failure ("detectors beat benchmarks yet OpenAI shut theirs down", Two Paradigms). 3-5 paragraphs + numbered contributions. P1: urgency/scale. P2: specific existing failures with numbers ("RoBERTa: 99.4→88.3 OOD", "variance collapse rarely a practical concern"). P3: approach + headline number. P4 (optional): method sketch. Contributions: 3 items (identify→analyze→validate pattern in 5/8). Exception: FineWeb uses single dense paragraph with 6 implicit contributions woven into prose. **Key rule**: quantified failure > vague criticism. Every tension paragraph cites a concrete number from prior work.

## Tension Strategies

Detection: **"works in lab, fails in wild"** (Ghostbuster, MAGE, Two Paradigms — 3/4 detection papers). Theory: **"right but practically wrong"** — prior theory valid but misses what practitioners observe (Closer Look: "variance collapse rarely practical"; Strong Collapse: "mixing doesn't fix it"). Detection: **problem_illustration** showing combinatorial challenge (domains×models, MAGE: many-to-many arrows). Method papers: **method_overview** pipeline (Ghostbuster: L→R pipeline; Closer Look: 3-row paradigm diagram). **Teaser_result** rare (1/8, Yi). Design consensus: horizontal L→R flow, pastel color-coding by conceptual layer, minimal text, real examples grounding abstract concepts. **Support**: 8/8, high confidence.

**Theory/collapse papers: zero tables** (4/4: Tale of Tails, Strong Collapse, Closer Look, Escaping Collapse). Detection main table pattern: rows=methods by_category, cols=grouped_by_dataset (ID+OOD side-by-side), bold_best, 4-10 baselines, **point estimates without std** (5/8 — std rare in this domain). **Support**: 8/8, high confidence.

Standard flow: motivation → main evidence → mechanism → ablation → extension. Key patterns: **paired qualitative+quantitative** panels (Closer Look: face grids + GS curves). **Parallel theory-experiment layout** (Tale of Tails). **Progressive difficulty as narrative arc** (MAGE: 8 testbeds easy→hard). **Discover-understand-mitigate-extend** (Closer Look: 3 findings + solution). **Ablation-as-narrative** (FineWeb: each pipeline stage = mini-experiment with hypothesis+result).

## Techniques Worth Stealing

1. **"Practical insufficiency"** (Closer Look): "prior work right but misses what matters in practice" — avoids direct conflict while establishing novelty. **Support**: 2/8, medium confidence, but effective pattern.
2. **Ablation-as-narrative** (FineWeb): pipeline stages as sequential mini-experiments. Counterintuitive findings (global dedup hurts) as dramatic peak. **Support**: 1/8 but universally applicable to pipeline papers.
3. **Promise-and-peril** (Escaping Collapse): short-term good news + long-term cautionary convergence. Nuanced > pure positive-result. **Support**: 1/8 but high novelty.
4. **Contradiction opener** (Two Paradigms): success vs failure juxtaposition in paragraph 1. **Support**: 2/8, medium confidence.
5. **Thought experiment** (Two Paradigms §3.3): iteratively add authors to show attribution breaks — makes theoretical argument viscerally intuitive. **Support**: 1/8 but highly memorable.

# AI Text Detection & Model Collapse — Research Patterns

From 25 papers (8 deep-read, 17 abstract). Domain: LLM text detection + model collapse + data quality.

## Method Trends

**Rising** (high confidence): Zero-shot statistical scoring dominates detection — DetectGPT→Fast-DetectGPT (340x speedup)→Binoculars (>90% TPR@0.01%FPR)→DivEye (+33.2%). Each successor simplifies and accelerates. Continuous/ordinal scoring replacing binary (EditLens regression, CLOC multi-margin). Detection-as-collapse-mitigation emerging: detector-filtered retraining outperforms pure human data (Drayson 2025). Verifier-based filtering shows short-term gains but converges to verifier's center (Yi 2026, Escaping Collapse).

**Declining**: Supervised binary classifiers fail OOD (MAGE: AUROC 0.99→0.93 cross-domain; Two Paradigms: attribution paradigm breaks at scale). Pure perturbation methods displaced by conditional probability approaches.

## Standard Baselines (citation freq)

DetectGPT (8/25) > RoBERTa-classifier (5/25) > Binoculars (4/25) ≈ Fast-DetectGPT (4/25) > Ghostbuster (3/25). New detectors must benchmark against Binoculars + Fast-DetectGPT as zero-shot SOTA, plus at least one supervised baseline. **Support**: 8/8 deep-read, high confidence.

## Metrics

**AUROC** dominant (12/25) but increasingly contested — Two Paradigms shows AUROC misleading under class imbalance, recommend supplementing with PR-AUC. **TPR@low-FPR** (0.01%-1%) preferred for deployment (Binoculars, Two Paradigms). **F1** for classification (6/25). Collapse domain: **FID** (4/25), **perplexity** (4/25), **test error scaling exponent** (3/25), **entropy** as diagnostic (Closer Look: r=0.91 with generalization). **Support**: 8/8, high confidence.

## Key Datasets

Detection: MAGE (7 domains×27 LLMs, 332K texts), RAID (2.6M texts, 6 LLMs), PAN'24 (15 LLMs). XSum/SQuAD/WritingPrompts = legacy trio (3/25 each). Collapse: CIFAR-10/FFHQ/MNIST for image (4/25), Wikitext-103/BabiStories for LM (2/25). Data quality: FineWeb 15T tokens, QuRating 260B.

## Experimental Design Consensus (6/8 deep-read)

1. Cross-domain + cross-model eval mandatory — in-domain results alone insufficient (MAGE, Two Paradigms, Ghostbuster)
2. Paraphrasing attack robustness required — universal weakness, recall drops 30-40% (MAGE, Ghostbuster, DivEye)
3. Progressive difficulty testbeds: easy→hard scenarios as narrative arc (MAGE: 8 testbeds; Two Paradigms: attribution→verification)
4. Collapse: iterate 8-60 rounds, report per-round FID/entropy/GS trajectory, not just final number
5. Training recipes: detection classifiers use Adam, lr~5e-3, 5 epochs on V100/A100; collapse theory uses closed-form or small DDPMs on single A100

## Common Limitations (cross-paper freq)

- Short text (<100 tokens): universal degradation (4/8 deep-read)
- Newest LLMs closing gap: GPT-4o entropy≈human beyond 4K chars; o1 undetectable by non-o1 detectors (Two Paradigms)
- Paraphrasing breaks all detectors (3/8; Ghostbuster 99%→62% recall)
- Collapse theory assumes Gaussian/linear — neural network gap acknowledged but unresolved (4/8)
- No instruction-tuned LLM collapse analysis across all papers

## Research Gaps

- **No paper estimates recursive generation depth** — detection is binary/ternary only; ordinal framing (EditLens, CLOC) exists but unapplied to depth
- Detection × collapse barely connected: only Drayson bridges; no work diagnoses *how many* generations occurred
- Strong Collapse proves mixing cannot fix collapse unless synthetic fraction→0, but no paper proposes depth-aware data curation
- Verifier quality bounds long-term performance (Yi 2026) — what if the verifier is a generation-depth estimator?

## Competitor Map

**Foundation** (9): DetectGPT, Two Paradigms, Tale of Tails, Strong Collapse, Closer Look, Broken Telephone, Ghostbuster, Demystified, survey. **Competitor** (6): MAGE, Binoculars, Fast-DetectGPT, DivEye, Intrinsic Dim, EditLens. **Complementary** (7): FineWeb, QuRating, Escaping Collapse, Drayson, Synthetic Eggs, LOKI, CLOC. **Orthogonal** (2): watermark, text degeneration.

# AI Text Detection & Model Collapse — Research Patterns

From 25 papers (8 deep-read, 17 abstract). Domain: LLM text detection + model collapse + data quality.

## Method Trends

**Rising** (high confidence): Zero-shot statistical scoring dominates detection — DetectGPT→Fast-DetectGPT (340x speedup)→Binoculars (>90% TPR@0.01%FPR)→DivEye (+33.2%). Each successor simplifies and accelerates. Continuous/ordinal scoring replacing binary (EditLens regression, CLOC multi-margin). Detection-as-collapse-mitigation emerging: detector-filtered retraining outperforms pure human data (Drayson 2025). Verifier-based filtering shows short-term gains but converges to verifier's center (Yi 2026, Escaping Collapse).

**Declining**: Supervised binary classifiers fail OOD (MAGE: AUROC 0.99→0.93 cross-domain; Two Paradigms: attribution paradigm breaks at scale). Pure perturbation methods displaced by conditional probability approaches.

## Standard Baselines (citation freq)

DetectGPT (8/25) > RoBERTa-classifier (5/25) > Binoculars (4/25) ≈ Fast-DetectGPT (4/25) > Ghostbuster (3/25). New detectors must benchmark against Binoculars + Fast-DetectGPT as zero-shot SOTA, plus at least one supervised baseline. **Support**: 8/8 deep-read, high confidence.

## Metrics

**AUROC** dominant (12/25) but increasingly contested — Two Paradigms shows AUROC misleading under class imbalance, recommend supplementing with PR-AUC. **TPR@low-FPR** (0.01%-1%) preferred for deployment (Binoculars, Two Paradigms). **F1** for classification (6/25). Collapse domain: **FID** (4/25), **perplexity** (4/25), **test error scaling exponent** (3/25), **entropy** as diagnostic (Closer Look: r=0.91 with generalization). **Support**: 8/8, high confidence.

## Key Datasets

Detection: MAGE (7 domains×27 LLMs, 332K texts), RAID (2.6M texts, 6 LLMs), PAN'24 (15 LLMs). XSum/SQuAD/WritingPrompts = legacy trio (3/25 each). Collapse: CIFAR-10/FFHQ/MNIST for image (4/25), Wikitext-103/BabiStories for LM (2/25). Data quality: FineWeb 15T tokens, QuRating 260B.

## Experimental Design Consensus (6/8 deep-read)

1. Cross-domain + cross-model eval mandatory — in-domain results alone insufficient (MAGE, Two Paradigms, Ghostbuster)
2. Paraphrasing attack robustness required — universal weakness, recall drops 30-40% (MAGE, Ghostbuster, DivEye)
3. Progressive difficulty testbeds: easy→hard scenarios as narrative arc (MAGE: 8 testbeds; Two Paradigms: attribution→verification)
4. Collapse: iterate 8-60 rounds, report per-round FID/entropy/GS trajectory, not just final number
5. Training recipes: detection classifiers use Adam, lr~5e-3, 5 epochs on V100/A100; collapse theory uses closed-form or small DDPMs on single A100

## Common Limitations (cross-paper freq)

- Short text (<100 tokens): universal degradation (4/8 deep-read)
- Newest LLMs closing gap: GPT-4o entropy≈human beyond 4K chars; o1 undetectable by non-o1 detectors (Two Paradigms)
- Paraphrasing breaks all detectors (3/8; Ghostbuster 99%→62% recall)
- Collapse theory assumes Gaussian/linear — neural network gap acknowledged but unresolved (4/8)
- No instruction-tuned LLM collapse analysis across all papers

## Research Gaps

- **No paper estimates recursive generation depth** — detection is binary/ternary only; ordinal framing (EditLens, CLOC) exists but unapplied to depth
- Detection × collapse barely connected: only Drayson bridges; no work diagnoses *how many* generations occurred
- Strong Collapse proves mixing cannot fix collapse unless synthetic fraction→0, but no paper proposes depth-aware data curation
- Verifier quality bounds long-term performance (Yi 2026) — what if the verifier is a generation-depth estimator?

## Competitor Map

**Foundation** (9): DetectGPT, Two Paradigms, Tale of Tails, Strong Collapse, Closer Look, Broken Telephone, Ghostbuster, Demystified, survey. **Competitor** (6): MAGE, Binoculars, Fast-DetectGPT, DivEye, Intrinsic Dim, EditLens. **Complementary** (7): FineWeb, QuRating, Escaping Collapse, Drayson, Synthetic Eggs, LOKI, CLOC. **Orthogonal** (2): watermark, text degeneration.
